text:
Ben A: Heads up — want to align on an artifact rotation playbook for on-prem installs that need per-component swap without a full-seed refresh. Thinking of calling it 'freezeback': freeze traffic briefly, stage components, swap atomically, verify, then thaw. Open to better names :thinking_face:

Maria (infra): Love the idea. Main worry: how do we ensure cross-component compatibility (minor tool/ABI mismatches) during a staggered swap? We need a preflight graph and a lightweight compatibility matrix.

Jamal (ops): +1. From ops side we need rollback <= 10m for tier-1 nodes. Proposed minimal ops steps: prebake artifact, stage as sidecar, swap symlink, run healthchecks, commit. Example dry-run command: `rdu admin rotate --component runtime --target v1.2.3 --dry-run`

Sylvia (eng-runtime): Avoid in-place overwrites of GPU libs — too risky. Prefer sidecar staging + atomic symlink switch. That limits kernel/lib link-flip windows.

Drew (sre): Operational suggestion: canary across 3 nodes with a 5m observation window, then parallelize per-rack. Add watchdog snapshot so rollback is guaranteed to an exact pre-swap state.

Ben A: Draft playbook sketch (high-level):
1) freeze ingress for target subset (iptables/conn-proxy redirect)
2) stage component as sidecar image or unpack into `/.staged/$component`
3) run smoke + perf probe (`curl /health && perf-check`)
4) atomically switch symlink (or k8s volume rename) to activate
5) monitor for 5m for errors/latency regressions
6) fallback via `freezeback rollback` which restores `symlink.snap` and restarts affected processes

deploy-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: sandbox run at 2024-08-22T15:00Z :calendar: (auto-notify ops channel)

Maria (infra): We should also standardize snapshot metadata: include `component`, `revision`, `sha256`, `abi_tag`, `qcow_flag` or equivalent. Pattern: `snapshot-$component-$rev-$sha256` so GC can easily target old snapshots.

Jamal (ops): Edge case: large model shards that can't be fully staged due to disk constraints. Options: 1) stream-activate (download-on-demand during activation window), 2) use a removable 'shadow-cache' device, 3) trigger partial activation with loader fallback. Not ideal but necessary in some deployments.

Sylvia (eng-runtime): For air-gapped customers signing matters. Staged artifacts must be signed and verifier embedded in operator image: `rdu verify --sig ./staged/snapshot-...`

Ben A: Another pattern: "lazy-activation" — upload/stage all blobs but keep components disabled until a single control-plane commit flips activation flag. This reduces downtime for huge blobs because activation window only covers final pointer swap.

Drew (sre): Concern: split-state between operator and orchestrator. Operator MUST be the single source of truth for activation state; otherwise we get races. Add leader-elected activation commits.

Maria (infra): Add TTL/GC policy for unreferenced staged artifacts: default `gc.unreferenced > 24h` then admin override. Also expose a `prune --dry-run` mode for audits.

Ben A: Quick example of snapshot manifest we could standardize (small):
```json
{"component":"runtime","rev":"v1.2.3","sha256":"abc123...","abi":"cuda12.1","signed":true}
```

Ben A: I'll write an RFC follow-up with a sequence diagram and a proposed k8s operator contract for stage/activate/rollback. Volunteers to review? @Sylvia @Drew

Sylvia (eng-runtime): I'll review — can do a pass on operator contract and compatibility checks. :thumbsup:

Jamal (ops): I'll run a dry-run on our air-gapped testbed next week and report timings for staging vs activation.

Drew (sre): Also suggest we capture metrics during dry-run: staging-time, activation-time, rollback-time, peak-disk-usage, latency delta. We'll need those to tune the canary window.

Ben A: Solid. Thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link when it's up and tag reviewers.
